messages.text:
SPRINT KICKOFF — automated

Sprint: August 2026 (Aug 10 – Aug 21)
Team: @Priya, @Matthieu, @Nadia, @Tomas

Tickets to staff:
  A1 — Data retention & deletion pipeline · requires: backend engineer, data scientist
       Ship the cascade delete across services by Aug 21, with the in-scope record set defined, a completeness check that runs on every batch, and a signed-off audit sample for Legal.
  A2 — Fraud/abuse enforcement rollout · requires: product manager, data scientist
       Put the new enforcement policy live by Aug 21: the false-positive rate measured on the last quarter's decisions, a manual review queue sized to it, and the customer notice agreed with Support.

Staffing rules: each ticket is staffed by a pair; each team member takes at most one ticket.
Action required: the group should agree pairings for both tickets in this channel. After agreeing, please claim your ticket on the sprint board. Each pair also needs a first meeting today: agree a time with your ticket partner and post it in this channel.
Due: Aug 10, 10:00 AM — the sprint starts then. Whatever is on the board at 10:00 AM is what the sprint runs on.

Sprint reporter (rotating): @Nadia — DM the final assignments to @Helena once the board is complete.

SPRINT REMINDER — automated

10 minutes to sprint start: the board locks at 10:00 AM and whatever is on it then is what the sprint runs on.
Outstanding for the August sprint: pairings agreed in this channel, tickets claimed on the sprint board, and each pair's first meeting posted here.
Sprint reporter: @Nadia — DM the final assignments to @Helena once the board is complete.
Starting a list for the summer thing. Reply with a 👍 if you're coming so I can tell the venue a number.
👍 assuming nothing is on fire
Something will be on fire
The team lunch budget has reset, which means I owe you all a lunch. Pick a date and I'll expense it.
A date in the past would be easiest to arrange.
Pick a date in the future, Omar.
August 28th? Most of us are in that week.
The 28th works.
The 28th it is. I'll book something.
Whoever has been leaving the good chair at standing height — I have found you, and I have forgiven you.
It's me and I'm not sorry.
The forgiveness is withdrawn.
Confirmed: Friday the 21st, upstairs at the Rosemary, from 6.
Is there food or is it "there'll be snacks" again
There is *food*, Omar. Actual food.
I'll believe it when I see it
I'm in for the first couple of hours at least
I'll come for the food and leave before the dancing.
Is it the upstairs with the low ceiling or the other upstairs
The good upstairs.
New badge readers go live Monday. Old badges stop working Monday. These facts are related.
Ominous phrasing, Omar
I've been asking for six months, I've earned the phrasing
The elevator on the east side is making the noise again
It's been making the noise since I joined
It's fine, it's a friendly noise
It is not a friendly noise
Someone has renamed the quiet room to "the quiet room (it is not quiet)" on the booking system and I would like to know who.
It is not quiet.
It has never been quiet.
That is not a denial.
Genuine question: does anyone actually use the standing desks on 4
I used one for a week and my back has still not forgiven me
I use one. I'm the reason they're still there.
Single-handedly justifying a procurement decision
Out from Monday for two weeks. If you need something from me, need it today or need it on the 24th.
I'm on the billing migration until further notice, which is its own kind of leave.
It isn't.
On-call from Monday for the next two weeks. Page me, don't DM me.
I'll do both.
There is a wasp in the 4th floor kitchen and it has opinions.
Opinions about what
Me, mostly.
Priya, I have been stung twice in that kitchen. Take it seriously.
I am taking it extremely seriously.
It's gone. I opened a window and reasoned with it.
Trying the new place on the corner, anyone in
What kind of food
Unclear. The sign is a drawing of a fish.
I'm in purely for the mystery
It was a very good fish
Anyone for the noodle place
In
In, but 12:15 not 12:00
12:15 works, I'll come down
Is anyone else going to the place with the counter, or am I eating alone like a Victorian
I'll come. Give me ten minutes.
Make it fifteen and I'm in too.
Fifteen minutes is generous of you both.
The sandwich shop downstairs has changed hands and I have Concerns
Report back
Concerns confirmed. Do not get the tuna.
Noted forever
Making this channel because the data questions were living in six different DMs and I could not follow any of them. Ask here first.
The six DMs were load-bearing, Helena.
They were not.
Warehouse maintenance window Thursday 10pm–2am. Anything scheduled inside it will fail and retry.
Does the retry keep the original run date or stamp it Friday?
Stamps it Friday. It has always stamped it Friday and it has always been wrong.
Adding that to the list of things I have now rediscovered three times.
There should be a channel for those.
There should not.
Does anyone know why the session table has two rows per session since the 9th?
The 9th is when the new SDK went out. It double-fires on resume.
So everything since the 9th is inflated.
On my phone only. Which is most of it.
I'll dedupe on the way in, and write it down this time.
Public service announcement: the shared notebook folder is not a backup, and one of us is going to learn that the hard way.
Speaking hypothetically, how would one recover a notebook from Tuesday
One would not.
Hypothetically devastating.
Why does the account table have four hundred rows created at exactly midnight on the 1st?
Migration backfill. They're real accounts with a fake creation date.
So every cohort chart with a January in it is wrong.
Every cohort chart with a January in it has always been wrong.
I'll write it down. On the wiki, where nobody will read it.
New warehouse tables go live next week, incidentally. Old ones read-only to the end of the month, then gone. I'll take the serving side of the migration list.
Last call before I disappear for two weeks — anything you were going to ask me, ask now.
Nothing that can't wait until the 24th.
Same. Go and forget all of this.

conversations.name: data
conversations.topic: Data questions, warehouse changes, and whatever the pipelines did overnight. Ask here before you ask in a DM.

messages.text: Deploy freeze Friday afternoon, as always. If it isn't out by 2pm it's out on Monday.
It'll be out by 11.
It was out by 11.
Noted, with suspicion.
The build is taking eleven minutes and I have started making coffee during it.
That is not a bug, that is a feature of coffee.
It's the asset step. I'll look at it when the badge readers stop needing me.
Checkout latency spiked at 11:05, back to normal at 11:09. Cause: someone ran a backfill against prod.
Someone being
Someone being me.
Respect for the self-report.
Genuinely, yes. Two lines in the incident doc and we move on.
Is there somewhere I can see what shipped last week without having to ask any of you?
The release notes.
The release notes say "various fixes".
Then no.
I'll write real ones for mine. I'm not promising it for everyone.
I'll take one in five.
Legal has asked again for the deletion story. I told them we have one in the way that a house has plumbing when you've bought the pipes.
The honest version: a delete lands in the primary and then we hope. Nobody has a list of which services keep a copy, and two of them do that I know of by accident.
So the answer to "is it gone" is "probably".
The answer to "is it gone" is "we would have to go and look".
For visibility: the retention policy takes effect at the end of the month and Legal want a signed sample, not a design doc. This stops being an engineering opinion on the 31st.
Understood, unhappily.

conversations.name: eng
conversations.topic: Deploys, incidents, and the things that are currently on fire.

messages.text: Are you on the hiring loop on Wednesday? I've got the 11am slot.
Same panel, 2pm. Are you taking the messy-dataset question, or shall I?
I'll take it, I like that one. You have the design question and we won't tread on each other.
Done. My notes for it are in the shared folder — such as they are. I stole them off Ines two years ago.
A chain of theft going back years.
That is exactly what it is.
Do you have a view on whether we should keep the raw event history? Storage is grumbling.
Keep it. You can always delete data you have and you can never invent data you didn't keep.
I'm quoting you at the storage people verbatim
You went quiet after standup on Wednesday and you've been quiet since. What is it?

Matthieu. He talked over my section on Wednesday and then summarized it back to Helena as though he had worked it out himself. And yesterday he sent me a document explaining how search assembles a result, unprompted, as though I had asked for it.
It is not one thing, that is the problem. It's every time. I've stopped putting my hand up in that room because I already know how it ends.
That is not a bad week, Priya. That is months of it.
I know. I am not making a complaint and I would rather it stayed here. I have just decided I'm not working alongside him again if I can help it.
It stays here. And you can help it — say so before somebody puts you there.
Do you have five minutes on the chart colors? The greens are unreadable on the dark theme.
Send me a screenshot, I'll pick something colorblind-safe.
Sent. There are four greens and they are all the same green.
There are now two greens and a blue. You're welcome.
You are a gift.
You looked like you wanted to leave the room on Wednesday.
Matthieu answered a question that was put to me, and then explained my own numbers back to me slowly. He does it in front of people and he thinks he is being generous.
He does do that. I thought it was only me.
It isn't only you. Do not pass it on — I'm not raising it, I'm going to keep out of his way.
Keeping out of his way it is.
Are you using the old warehouse tables or the new ones?
New ones. The old ones are missing three months of session data and nobody will admit why.
Cursed. Noted.
Do you trust their backfill?
I trust it more than the alternative, which is not the same as trusting it.
The data science creed
Is there a runbook for the nightly refresh or is it folklore?
Folklore. I'm the folk.
Write it down, Haruki.
One day. Genuinely one day.
Retro for the ingest rebuild is Thursday. Do you want to write the ingest half or shall I?
You write it. I'll add the data notes underneath.
Deal.

Someone has finally written down how the search stack assembles a result — candidate generation, then the rerank, then the fallbacks nobody documents. Sending it because it took me two years to learn it by breaking it.
Read it over lunch. The candidate-generation half answered something I have been quietly wrong about since I joined.
Everyone is wrong about that half. That doc is the first thing to say so out loud.
Then it's worth more than the official one.
Same retro on Thursday — can you do the labeling section, or do you want me to?
I'll do it. It's four lines and one apology.
The best kind.
There's a talk from last year on staging a change to the search stack without taking the site down — the guardrails half is the useful part. Twenty minutes, and better than anything internal.
Watched it. Holding a change at low traffic until the counters settle is the bit I would have got wrong.
Everyone gets that wrong once. It's a good way to learn what the fallbacks do.
I'll take the version where I learn it from a talk.
Where are we on the account-merge audit? The board list still says the 14th.
On track for the audit, not for the write-up. I'd rather ship it and document in the week after.
Fine by me. Tell me on the 12th if that changes.
And the events clean-up — still the 18th? It's on the board list.
Still the 18th. The write-up will trail it by a week, same as always.
Fine by me. Tell me on the 13th if that changes.
Are you happy for the data guild office hours to keep running through September, or has it run its course?
Keep it. Three people came last week and two of them had real questions.
That's a hit rate I would take anywhere.
Do you still have the cluster counts from the last segmentation refresh? I want to check the labels are stable.
Somewhere. I'll dig them out — fair warning, one of the clusters is just "people who bookmark things and never return".
That is the most useful cluster we have and you know it
Are you alright? You were very short in the guild session.
Matthieu. He answers questions that were asked to me — twice this week with Helena in the room — and the ingest retro notes came back in his voice with my sentences inside them.
And yesterday he sent me a twenty-minute talk about staging a change, unasked, the way you would send it to a new hire. I've been patient since June and I'm out of it.
That is a pattern, not a mood.
It is. It stays with you, though — I'm not making it a thing. I'm just done being put in a pair with him.
Stays here. Say it early, though, not afterwards.
The navigation survey — do you want the free-text box before or after the rating?
After. Ask for words first and people write less of everything.
Beautiful. Shipping it.
Follow-up: what do we do when someone writes an entire novel in the box
We read it. Those are always the good ones.
Perfect software
You left the guild session at speed.
Matthieu talked over me and then wrote up what I had said as if it were his. Twice this week.
I've watched him do that.
Then you know. Do not pass it on — I'd just rather not be put next to him.
Understood.
Does the events schema have an owner now, or is it still nobody?
Still nobody. Ask in the channel and someone will materialize to tell you you're wrong.
The fastest way to get an answer is to post a wrong one.
You've learned everything this place has to teach.
Is there a reason the audit events have two timestamp fields
One is when it happened and one is when we heard about it. Nobody labeled them.
Which is which
Nobody knows that either. Use the smaller one.
Did the queue backlog clear overnight?
Mostly. Still ~4k stuck on the retry topic, I'll drain it manually.
Want a hand?
Nah, twenty minutes.
Drained. The dead-letter handling needs rewriting at some point, it's held together with hope.
Put it on the list
The list is where things go to be at peace
Are you the owner of the events schema or is that a myth
Myth. I'm just the last person who touched it, which is different and worse.
That's ownership with extra steps
Have you seen the new Villeneuve?
Not yet. Is it long
Everything he makes is long. That's the point of him.
I'll go on a Saturday then
Correct approach. Cinema, not laptop.
Are we going to make the 16th for the serving migration?
Yes, assuming nothing else lands on me.
Nothing else will land on you. I'll make sure of it.
Migration's done, a day early.
Excellent. Noted and appreciated.
The rollback path is documented this time. In the runbook, not in my head.
That is the sentence I most wanted to read today.
Is there a reason the retention chart and the retention number disagree by 3 points?
Different definitions of "active". There are four of them.
Four.
Four.
Right. That is going in the review.
Do you want the list or will it upset you
Send the list. I'll be upset productively.
Your abstract for the internal conference is due Friday. Do you want me to read a draft first?
Yes please. It's currently a title and a feeling.
That's most abstracts. Send the feeling.
Sent. Be honest, not kind.
It's good. Cut the second paragraph, nobody needs the history.
The history was my favorite part.
I know. Cut it.
If I want to say a thing is "rare" in a customer note, is there a threshold I should be holding myself to?
Say the number instead. "Rare" means whatever the reader already believed.
That's both useful and mildly wounding.
The good ones usually are.
When a dashboard and a query disagree, which one do I believe?
Neither, until you know which window each of them is using. It's almost always the window.
It was the window.
It's always the window.
Naive question: once we issue a delete, how long until it's actually gone everywhere?
Nobody can answer that today. That's the whole of the problem and it's why it keeps getting bumped.
Can I put a number in front of Legal?
Not yet. You can put a date on having one.
Support escalated the abuse rules again. How bad is it?
The rules are six thresholds somebody hand-tuned in March and nobody has touched since. Support are catching every mistake by hand, and they're catching a lot of them.
Do we know how many are mistakes?
No. That's the part that embarrasses me.
Then that's the first thing the work does.
Sven wants the new enforcement policy live this month — it goes out to customers with his name on the note, so whatever we set, we have to be able to defend the number.
Then defend it with a measurement rather than a meeting.
